newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's Zeroual meets politicians on election.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Zeroual meets politicians on election.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual held talks with seven party leaders on Tuesday to discuss when local elections planned for this year should take place, the official Algerian news agency APS said.

The main moderate Islamist Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS), which is represented in the coalition government with Zeroual's supporters and former ruling National Liberation Front (FLN), was not at the meeting, officials said.
Secular opposition parties, the Socialist Forces Front (FFS) and Rally for Culture and Democracy (RCD), also did not attend the meeting with Zeroual.
The three parties want more transparency and say in the process of controlling the poll to limit what they see as massive cheating which they said marred last month's general elections.
The authorities denied there was widespread abuse and said the balloting had been free and fair.

The National Democratic Rally (RND), grouping Zeroual's backers, the FLN, Islamist-oriented Nahda, left-wing Workers' Party, Progressive Republican Party, Union for Democracy and Freedom, and the Social Liberal Party leaders took part in the meeting with Zeroual, said APS.
The parties are among the 10 political groups represented in the 380-member National Assembly (lower house) elected last month.
Late in June, Zeroual and his aides met party leaders for similar discussions.
A cross-party working group has been set up to study preparations of the local elections and the work of a planned independent commission to supervise the poll.

The meeting was held just hours after the authorities set free radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) chief Abassi Madani who was sentenced by a military court in July 1992 to 12 years' jail for threatening Algeria's security.
The main opposition party leaders had urged Zeroual to free FIS leaders as a step towards stopping violence and helping national understanding after five and half years of strife.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since 1992 when the authorities cancelled the first multi-party general election in which FIS had taken a huge lead.
